role: AK_TEXT (lines and table rows); MODERN_EDITORIAL (the editor's numbers, brackets, note marks and folio references; his footnotes not reproduced)
comment: Frame 112, printed p. 106: the heading of the springs beyond the equator, damaged in the manuscript, and its one spring, from the mountain الّهه to the sea in the first clime; then the Nile of Egypt, under a heading the editor adds: the two round lakes and the five rivers from the mountain of the Moon that flow into the first lake, and the beginning of the five that flow into the second. The editor's running numbers (١٦٠٤)-(١٦١٧) and the numbers of Suhrāb [٢٢٣٠]-[٢٢٣٢] and [١٥٠٣]-[١٥١٣]; the folio of the manuscript, «(fol. 30ᵃ)», at the beginning of the heading. Seven lines of the editor's footnotes.

lines.plain: عند نز ك (١٦١٦) [١٥١٢] والرابع عند ٮح ك (١٦١٧) [١٥١٣] والخامس عند

variants: L01: the manuscript has a gap in the heading; the editor reads the remains as apparently اسماء, names, though by the headings of the following chapters one would expect والأنهار (note a).
L01: the manuscript is badly damaged at the bracketed letters (note b).
L02: the manuscript lacks the word خلف; the editor supplies it (note c).
L05: the manuscript has no heading for the Nile; the editor adds it for clarity (note d).
L06, L07: the manuscript writes the number five, خمسة, as the numeral ه, 5, with a line over it, printed in the two-eyed form of the letter drawn with two triangles (note e).
L09: the manuscript lacks the word طول; the editor supplies it (note f).
L09: the ن of the longitude of the third river is written by a later hand in the manuscript (note g).
L11: the manuscript writes خمسة as the numeral ه with a line over it, as at note e (note h).

L13: the manuscript has ن ل for the longitude of the third river, and a variant reading is ٮو ل, a tooth without a dot joined to the و, each with a line over the numerals; the editor corrects it in view of the second and the fourth river, points 1615 and 1617 (note i).
unresolved: L07: the notched form may also be read as a single ر whose head is split, ر, 7. Transcribed ٮر.
observations: The places in which the boundaries of the countries are written end on p. 105 (frame 111), whose last entry closes fol. 29ᵃ of the Strasbourg manuscript; fol. 29ᵇ is blank (frame 111, note u). The folio «(fol. 30ᵃ)» is printed in Latin type at the beginning of the heading, before its star; transcribed as a margin note before the line.

L01: the heading of the next section, in larger type: «* ار⟨. . . . .⟩ا ا⟨لعيون⟩ الّتى خلف خطّ الاستواء *», the … of the springs beyond the equator. Its first word is printed «ار», an alif and a small ر, then a gap of five evenly spaced dots between angle brackets, followed by the note mark a, then a final alif whose joining stroke runs out to the right at its foot; after a space, an alif, and «لعيون» between angle brackets, followed by the note mark b. The editor's note a says that the gap appears to hold اسماء, names, though by the headings of the following chapters one would expect والأنهار, and the rivers; note b, that the manuscript is badly damaged there. Transcribed with the dots and the brackets, as printed. «الّتى» has a shadda over the ل and «خطّ» a shadda over the ط; a small open star with six points stands at each end of the heading.

L02-L04: «عين تخرج من جبل الّهه من ⟨خلف⟩ خطّ الاستواء من طول ل ل وعرض ه {z} (١٦٠٤)», a spring that comes out of the mountain الّهه from beyond the equator, from the longitude 30° 30′ and the latitude 5° 0′; «فتمرّ الى طول كز {z} وعرض ح ل (١٦٠٥)» (L03), and it passes to the longitude 27° 0′ and the latitude ح ل; «ثمّ تمرّ الى البحر فى الإقليم الأوّل عند طول ٮط {z} وعرض و ى (١٦٠٦)» (L03-L04), then it passes to the sea in the first clime at the longitude ٮط {z} and the latitude 6° 10′. Here «وعرض» stands where the other sections have «والعرض». «الّهه» has a shadda over the ل; the table of the mountains prints the name «الهه» (frame 044, entry 548/549). «⟨خلف⟩» stands between angle brackets, followed by the note mark c: the manuscript lacks the word, and the editor supplies it (note c).

L05-L13: the Nile of Egypt. «⟨نيل مصر وما يقع اليه من العيون والأنهار⟩» (L05), the Nile of Egypt and the springs and rivers that fall into it, is set between angle brackets at the beginning of the line, in the type of the text, followed by the note mark d: the manuscript has no heading there, and the editor adds it for clarity (note d). Then «بطيحتان مدوّرتان قطر كلّ واحدة خمسة اجزاء مركز الأولى عند طول ں {z} والعرض ر {z} (١٦٠٧) ومركز الثانية عند طول ٮر {z} والعرض ر {z} (١٦٠٨)» (L05-L07), two round lakes, the diameter of each five degrees, the centre of the first at the longitude ں {z} and the latitude ر {z}, and the centre of the second at the longitude ٮر {z} and the latitude ر {z}; «ينصبّ الى الأولى خمسة انهار من جبل القمر» (L07-L08), into the first flow five rivers from the mountain of the Moon, whose beginnings are given by their longitudes only, «مبتدأ النهر الأوّل عند طول مح {z}», 48° 0′, «والثانى عند ⟨طول⟩ مط {z}», 49° 0′, «والثالث عند طول ن {z}», 50° 0′, «والرابع عند طول نا {z}», 51° 0′, «والخامس عند طول نب {z}», 52° 0′ (points 1609-1613); and «ويخرج من جبل القمر ايضًا خمسة انهار الى البطيحة الثانية» (L11), from the mountain of the Moon come five more rivers to the second lake, «مبتدأ النهر الأوّل عند طول نه ك», 55° 20′, then «والثانى عند ٮو ك», «والثالث عند نز ك», «والرابع عند ٮح ك» (L12-L13), without «طول», and «والخامس عند», continued on p. 107 (points 1614-1617).

The running numbers run (١٦٠٤)-(١٦١٧) without a gap. The numbers of Suhrāb are [٢٢٣٠]-[٢٢٣٢] for the spring, after (١٦٠٤)-(١٦٠٦), [٢٢٣٠] at the beginning of L03, and [١٥٠٣]-[١٥١٣] for the Nile, after (١٦٠٧)-(١٦١٧), [١٥٠٩] at the beginning of L11. Each section ends with a small open star with six points, transcribed as an asterisk (L04, L05, L07, L11).

L09: «⟨طول⟩», between angle brackets, followed by the note mark f: the manuscript lacks the word, and the editor supplies it (note f). L09: the note mark g stands within the line over the numerals of the third river, between the ن and the zero: the ن is written by a later hand in the manuscript (note g).

Signs in the text, transcribed as printed: «الّتى», «الّهه» with a shadda over the ل; «خطّ» (L01, L02), «فتمرّ», «تمرّ» and «ثمّ» (L03), «كلّ» (L05) and «ينصبّ» (L07) with a shadda; «مدوّرتان» (L05) with a shadda over the و; «الأوّل» (L04, L08, L12) with a hamza over the alif and a shadda over the و; «الإقليم» (L04) with a hamza below the alif; «الأولى» (L06, L07) and «والأنهار» (L05) with a hamza over the alif; «مبتدأ» (L08, L11) with a hamza over the alif; «اجزاء» with a hamza on the line; «ايضًا» (L11) with the tanwīn of the accusative over the alif; «الأولى», «الثانى» and «فى» end in a ى without dots.

Numerals: «ل ل» (L02), 30° 30′; «ه {z}» (L02), the small round form of the isolated ه, 5° 0′; «كز» (L03), with the dot of the ز, 27; «ح ل» (L03), 8° 30′; «و ى» (L04), 6° 10′; «مح» (L08), 48, «مط» (L09), 49, «ن» (L09), «نا» and «نب» (L10), with the dot of the ن and, in «نب», the dot of the ب below, 50, 51 and 52; «نه ك» (L12), with the dot of the ن over the tooth, 55° 20′; «نز ك» (L13), with the dots of the ن and of the ز, 57° 20′. Without their dots, transcribed so: «ٮط» (L04), a tooth joined to a ط, which read with a ي gives 19 and read as a ن 59; «ں» (L06), the bowl of a final ن without its dot, 50; «ٮو ك» (L12) and «ٮح ك» (L13), a tooth joined to a و and to a ح, which read as a ن give 56° 20′ and 58° 20′, between 55° 20′ and 57° 20′ and after 57° 20′.

In these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed: «ر» (L06, L07, the degrees of the latitudes of the two lakes), a single rounded stroke, 7. L07, the degrees of the longitude of the second lake: the notched form ٮر of frame 041 (L06), a short tooth without a dot joined to a ر, the two forming a notch, 3 px deep, at the top, where the latitudes of L06 and L07 are single strokes; transcribed ٮر, which read as نز gives 57, beside the longitude 50° 0′ of the first lake and the longitudes 55° 20′-58° 20′ of the rivers that flow into the second.

The ح of «ح ل» (L03), «مح» (L08) and «ٮح» (L13) shows no dot in the bowl; the same form is a ج without its dot, 3. Transcribed as printed. The isolated ى, 10 (L04), has no dots. The isolated ك, 20, is printed with the small inner stroke of the letter (L12, L13).

Note marks: L01, a after the closing angle bracket of the gap and b after that of «⟨لعيون⟩»; L02, c after «⟨خلف⟩»; L05, d after the closing angle bracket; L06, e after «خمسة»; L07, e after «خمسة»; L09, f after «⟨طول⟩» and g within the line over the numerals; L11, h after «خمسة»; L13, i after the numerals of the third river.
The editor's footnotes stand in seven lines below a short rule at the left: notes a-i. The page number «— ١٠٦ —» stands at the foot, centred, on the line that ends note i.
